issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking statutory protection from eviction for rent arrears must make the required deposit within the period measured from the tenant’s knowledge of the pending suit when the suit was filed after the statutory regime took effect; later knowledge of the building’s construction date does not extend that period.
material_facts: The eviction suit for rent arrears was filed after the Act had come into force.
The tenants contested the suit and claimed the protection available to tenants in arrears.
The tenants knew the suit was pending but did not deposit the arrears within one month of acquiring that knowledge.
The tenants later sought information about the building’s construction date and deposited the arrears in April 1976.
The tenants gave no explanation for failing to deposit within one month of learning that the suit was pending.
issues.conclusion: The deposit was not timely under Section 39, and the tenants could not claim its protection. The High Court’s order was set aside and the eviction decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 39 of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 permits the required deposit within one month from commencement of the Act or within one month from the tenant’s knowledge of the pendency of the suit, whichever is later. Where the Act had taken effect before the suit was filed, the relevant trigger was knowledge of the suit’s pendency. The section does not make knowledge of the building’s construction date a trigger. The Court relied on the text of Section 39; it also agreed with Vineet Kumar v. Mangal Sain Wadhera that the relevant observation in Om Prakash v. Digvijendrapal was obiter, without needing to decide the Act’s application to a suit not pending when the Act commenced.

rule.if: eviction_suit_for_rent_arrears and tenant_sought_statutory_arrears_relief and suit_filed_after_regime_took_effect and tenant_knew_suit_was_pending and deposit_made_after_suit_knowledge_deadline and tenant_waited_for_building_age_information

predicates.eviction_suit_for_rent_arrears: A landlord brought an eviction suit seeking recovery of premises on the ground of rent arrears.
predicates.tenant_sought_statutory_arrears_relief: The tenant claimed statutory protection available to tenants who were in arrears of rent.
predicates.suit_filed_after_regime_took_effect: The landlord filed the eviction suit after the relevant rent-control regime had taken effect.
predicates.tenant_knew_suit_was_pending: The tenant knew that the eviction suit was pending.
predicates.deposit_made_after_suit_knowledge_deadli: The tenant deposited the required arrears only after the period running from knowledge of the pending suit had expired.
predicates.tenant_waited_for_building_age_informati: The tenant waited for information about the building’s construction date before making the deposit.

issues.definition: When a tenant claims statutory arrears protection in an eviction suit filed after the relevant regime took effect, knows the suit is pending, deposits only after the period measured from that knowledge, and waits for building-age information, the tenant does not obtain that protection.

issues.legal_issue: A statement in an earlier decision that the statutory tenant-protection provision applied only to suits pending when the Act commenced was obiter when that question was unnecessary to the earlier decision.
material_facts: The Court considered an earlier decision in which the building had not yet reached the age at which it would come within the Act’s coverage when the revision was heard.
The earlier decision’s outcome therefore did not require deciding whether the statutory protection applied only to suits pending when the Act commenced.
A later decision had treated the earlier statement as obiter, and the Court agreed with that characterization.
issues.conclusion: The Court agreed that the earlier statement about suits pending at commencement was obiter dicta. It did not decide whether the statutory protection applied to a suit that was not pending when the Act commenced.
issues.legal_principle: The Court followed Vineet Kumar v. Mangal Sain Wadhera in treating the statement in Om Prakash v. Digvijendrapal as obiter because it was unnecessary to resolve that case: the building had not become ten years old when the revision was heard. Although Nand Kishore Marwah v. Samundri Devi was cited in argument, the Court expressly found it unnecessary to decide the applicability of Section 39 to suits not pending at commencement.

predicates.prior_tenant_protection_case: An earlier case concerned whether a tenant could claim statutory protection from eviction.
predicates.building_not_yet_within_protection_age: The building in the earlier case had not yet reached the age required to come within the statutory protection when the revision was heard.
predicates.prior_court_did_not_need_to_decide_pendi: The earlier case could be resolved without deciding whether protection depended on the suit being pending when the regime commenced.

issues.definition: When an earlier tenant-protection case involved a building not yet within the protection’s age threshold and did not need to decide the pending-suit question, its statement on that question is obiter.
